key_insight: A training-free attribution method (Masked Prediction Distribution, MPD) can expose and correct two systematic errors—precision bias from high-resolution screens and ambiguity bias from complex UI elements—improving GUI grounding performance without retraining.
problem_solved: GUI grounding models struggle in complex, high-resolution, and cluttered interfaces (e.g., ScreenSpot-Pro) because they exhibit precision and ambiguity biases that lead to incorrect click/drag targets.
method: Introduce MPD (Masked Prediction Distribution) to attribute model predictions by measuring how masked image regions change the model's output distribution.
Diagnose two dominant failure modes: precision bias (high-res leads to localization errors) and ambiguity bias (complex interface elements cause confusion).
Apply training-free mitigation strategies informed by MPD (e.g., targeted masking/score recalibration and candidate re-ranking) to correct predictions post-hoc.
impact: Enables practitioners to analyze and reduce systematic grounding errors quickly and cheaply—improving reliability of GUI agents in real-world, complex interfaces without expensive retraining cycles.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: original GUI -> MPD masking grid -> prediction distributions -> mitigation step
Side-by-side example: before vs after mitigation showing corrected click targets on a high-resolution screen
Bar chart: error rates by bias type (precision vs ambiguity) before and after BAMI
Iconography: resolution meter and clutter/element complexity icons to represent the two bias sources
paper_title: BAMI: Training-Free Bias Mitigation in GUI Grounding
paper_authors: Borui Zhang, Bo Zhang, Bo Wang, Wenzhao Zheng, Yuhao Cheng
